source.title: Multiple Descents in Deep Learning as a Sequence of Order-Chaos Transitions in LSTM Networks
source.authors: Wenbo Wei; Fan Xu; N. Le; Choy Heng Lai; Ling Feng

record.tranche_reason: The study reports repeated training-time test-loss descents in LSTMs and argues that this multiple-descent pattern differs from the previously described epoch-wise double descent, while leaving their relationship unresolved.
record.gate_note: The paper reports test-loss curves and their relation to stability measures. It also says accuracy changes little across large loss swings. It does not sweep model size or training sample count. The reported asymptotic distances and FTLE values are used to analyze order-chaos transitions, not as test-error results.
record.test_reason: The study tracks test loss over 1,000 training epochs of LSTMs, a new setting with no label noise. It reports repeated rise-then-drop cycles in test loss, which bear on the epoch-wise shape V2 describes. The authors do not argue V2 is wrong; they say the relationship to epoch-wise double descent is unresolved. So T3 fits better than T5.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly right. More precisely, the authors claim that each test-loss descent in overtrained LSTMs coincides with an order-chaos transition, and that the best epoch is the first order-to-chaos transition. They also say multiple descents need no label noise and are abrupt rather than smooth, unlike epoch-wise double descent. Whether the two phenomena are connected is left open.
record.recipe_differences: This study trains an LSTM on sentiment analysis and tracks test loss and dynamical stability across epochs; it does not reproduce the original model-size or sample-size double-descent sweeps.
record.method_sensitivity: Multiple descents vary with learning rate, model size, optimizer, dataset, and random seed. The authors report that low learning rate or smaller size can leave the model ordered without multiple descents, and that SGD does not show the multiple-descent pattern in the reported experiments.

fits_no_version.finding: Repeated abrupt test-loss descents during overtraining of LSTMs without label noise, each coinciding with an order-chaos transition (FTLE sign change). The global optimum is at the first order-to-chaos transition.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Epoch-wise multiple descent in recurrent networks tracks order-chaos phase transitions of the network dynamics.

record.peer_reviewed: Physica A: Statistical Mechanics and its Applications
record.problems: The main analysis uses one LSTM task and reports test loss rather than a test-error curve; the authors state that accuracy changes little despite large loss swings. Asymptotic analysis uses a 500-review test subset. Measurements are made once per epoch, and the authors note that narrow transitions can fall between epochs. The compared Yelp settings change learning rate and model size together.
record.rows_left_out: No individual rows were extracted from Supplementary Figures S1–S14, which are presented as plots without separate textual outcome descriptions for each configuration; the reported aggregate SGD statement is captured in r5. Other random-seed traces are described as similar, with best epochs varying, but no separate numeric outcomes are stated.

untested.parts: Test-error (0-1) curves with numbers; dependence on label noise (no noise added); interaction with model size beyond the confounded two-setting Yelp comparison.
No model-size sweep around an interpolation threshold.
No capacity sweeps across model classes.
No effective-complexity measure tested against peak location.
Label noise and regularization are not varied; multiple descents appear without label noise, but this is not a controlled test.

missing.what: The global best epoch is the first minimum (epoch 114, accuracy 88.34%). Later descents are only local optima and never beat it. This bears on whether the second descent improves on the first.
Additional IMDb seeds also show multiple descents, with best epochs at 190 and 120, each at the first order-to-chaos transition.
Per-configuration test accuracies for Supplementary runs (e.g., IMDb Adam 0.867–0.884; Yelp 0.793–0.814; SGD 0.850–0.872), with descent presence shown only in plots.

record.verdict_notes: The measure throughout is test loss; accuracy barely moves, so the results speak to loss-based rather than error-based epoch-wise curves. A second V2 verdict is not encodable in the labels field due to an output-format error: limits_scope for IMDb LSTM-1 (Adam, learning rate 0.0005, test accuracy and loss), rows r1 and r2. The reason: test loss shows the rise-drop cycles, but later descents never beat the first minimum and accuracy does not follow them. A third verdict is likewise not encodable: limits_scope for Yelp with learning rate 0.0003 and hidden dimension 60, and for IMDb SGD runs, rows r3 and r5. The reason: no descents occur (0 of 10 seeds in r3, none with SGD in r5), so the cycles depend on learning rate, model size and optimizer. The r3 versus r4 comparison confounds learning rate with hidden size. Appendix C says intermediate settings give mixed results, and these were not reported. The Fig. 9 caption contradicts Table 2. Neither study is an original source.

versions.untested_parts: No controlled model-size sweep measuring test error around an interpolation threshold.
The study reports test loss rather than a full test-error or accuracy curve; it does not establish the canonical single fall-rise-fall curve.
No training-sample-size sweep near an interpolation threshold.
No evaluation across model classes or capacity sweeps.
The study relates training-time losses to order-chaos transitions but does not test whether one effective-complexity measure predicts peak location across axes.
The study does not systematically vary label noise or tune regularization; its discussion of noise and regularization is not a test of their dependence.
No alternative effective-parameter count is evaluated.

rows.subject: LSTM-1
rows.size_stated: Embedding dimension 32; LSTM output dimension 60; fully connected output dimension 1
rows.operation_detail: Train across epochs while measuring test loss

conditions.value: 30% of dataset; 500 reviews sampled for asymptotic analysis

rows.value: The paper reports 8 visible cycles of rising test loss followed by an abrupt drop within one epoch between epochs 500 and 1000.
rows.note: This is repeated, abrupt multiple descent in test loss, rather than a reported single canonical fall-rise-fall test-error curve.
rows.check: Baseline should be the first test-loss minimum at epoch 114 (accuracy 88.34%), which the authors say is the global best. The later descents are only local optima and never recover it. The shape is a fall-rise followed by many abrupt rise-drop cycles in loss, not a single second descent. Partial is correct.

rows.subject: LSTM-1
rows.size_stated: Embedding dimension 32; LSTM output dimension 60; fully connected output dimension 1
rows.operation_detail: Compare test accuracy behavior with the loss swings during overtraining

conditions.value: approximately 75 of 500 reviews; exact number varies

rows.measure: Test accuracy / incorrect predictions alongside test-loss changes
rows.baseline: Test loss varies substantially across the cycles
rows.value: The authors state that large test-loss changes do not produce similar changes in accuracy and do not mean significantly more incorrect predictions.
rows.note: This result qualifies the test-loss pattern: it is not accompanied by comparable changes in classification accuracy.
rows.check: This is the closest row to V2's test-error measure. Accuracy does not follow the loss cycles, and the authors report no significant rise in incorrect predictions. No numbers are given; the claim is text only.

relation.reason: Its own experiments measure test-loss trajectories across training epochs and compare their behavior across settings and with classification accuracy.

tranche.reason: The study reports temporal generalization-loss curves in a new LSTM sentiment-analysis setting. Its multiple descents bear on V2; the authors leave their relationship to conventional epoch-wise double descent unresolved.

source_check.notes: A counted descent requires a single-epoch test-loss drop of at least 1 after 20 epochs of continuous increase; it is not a count of classification-error cycles. Figure 9's sentence claiming multiple descents contradicts its heading, Table 2 and Appendix C, which establish zero descents for that setting.
